decisions.reason: The ID Vault was announced publicly with a press release as a groundbreaking feature and fits the super-app identity ecosystem, so dropping it within a year would expose the launch as a mistake, though as a feature it could be quietly folded into the platform.

The wallet is only mentioned and overlaps with the dedicated payment framework, so it could be merged away at little cost, but it remains tied to the firm's identity-bound payment narrative and early results can still be blamed on market timing.

The NFC tag authenticator is a peripheral hardware-style add-on with only a passing mention and little visible commitment, so little is lost and nothing has to be justified by dropping it to refocus on the platform.
The payment and wallet framework has its own page and is a core building block of the announced secure super-app ecosystem, so sunk investment and public commitment favor persisting with it.

As the flagship super-app platform that is central to the firm's announced strategic direction, withdrawing it would write off major investment and contradict its public positioning, so any weak results will be attributed to temporary adoption delays.

The application shielding library builds on the firm's decades of patented app-security expertise, has its own page, and supports the platform's security promise, making it a well-anchored product to keep.
